sections.h2: Which Brandenburg offices matter for a Meade County tax bill?
sections.html:
Most of the work happens in two suites at 516 Hillcrest Drive. Suite 3 houses the Property Valuation Administration (PVA), reachable at (270) 422-2178 on weekdays between eight and four-thirty. Suite 14 is the Sheriff's Office, where payments are taken, at (270) 422-4937.

Value is one office's business and collection is the other's. Take exemption and value questions to Suite 3, and take a bill in hand to Suite 14. Only after April 15, when unpaid bills transfer, does the County Clerk come into it.

sections.h2: How and when do Meade County residents pay?
sections.html:
Pay the Sheriff. The 2026 bills went into the mail on Friday, October 30, 2026, and a notice dated November 4 conceded that many owners still had not received theirs. It directed them to an online lookup of 2026 tax information so the amount could be checked while the mail caught up.

  • The statute, KRS 134.015, gives 2 percent off for payment by November 1. Because the 2026 bills only left October 30, ask the Sheriff which dates apply; the law permits a different schedule when mailing is delayed.
  • Through December 31, the printed figure is due.
  • January brings 5 percent.
  • After January it is 10 percent.
  • April 15 closes collection; in 2026 the last in-person payment was due at the counter by 4:30 p.m.

One rule trips up late payers. For the final two weeks of every collection period, the Sheriff declines personal checks, so cash, debit or credit cards, money orders and cashier's checks are the options. The office describes this as a yearly custom, with personal checks accepted again earlier in future seasons.

sections.h2: What does a typical Meade County house owe?
sections.html:
The Census figure for a middle-of-the-road owned home is $207,900, above McCracken County's $188,100. At Frankfort's 2025 rate of 10.6 cents per $100, the state takes about $220.37 on such a house. Levies from the county, the school district and special districts are set apart and added.

The county nearly doubled between 1950 and 1960 and has kept climbing:

The July 2025 estimate is 30,699, up 2.3 percent on 2020. Median rent is $1,026, median household income $74,355, and builders took out 165 permits in 2025. Employment grew 6.2 percent from 2022 to 2023, to 3,633 jobs at 362 employer establishments, and retail sales reached about $305 million in 2022.

sections.h2: Is there a homestead exemption in Meade County?
sections.html:
Yes. For 2025 and 2026, a homeowner 65 or older, or totally disabled, has $49,100 subtracted from assessed value. On the $207,900 median that leaves $158,800 taxable and a state share near $168.33.

The Meade County PVA set May 22, 2026 as the filing date for the exemption to show on the November bill, and that date is past. Residents who turn 65 in a later year should ask the office for that year's cutoff. Prompt filing also lets taxing districts plan budgets and rates, the PVA notes. A birth certificate, driver's license or passport proves age. Applicants claiming disability need a government or retirement-plan finding of total disability and must renew yearly, apart from service-connected veterans and holders of a permanent finding from Social Security or the Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: How does a Meade County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
Start with a meeting at the PVA; Kentucky takes appeals only from owners who had one. At it, the PVA must go over the rules and the way your value was set.

  • Public viewing of the roll lasts 13 days from the first Monday in May, with the dates advertised.
  • Your appeal must reach the County Clerk before closing on the day following the end of viewing.
  • Attach evidence: land and building details, insurance, construction cost and sale listings. Appeals without it are denied.
  • The local board of assessment appeals hears cases roughly a month after viewing, for no more than five days unless the state grants an extension.

Audio recording of the hearing is your right. A value set above your claim after bills were printed produces a supplemental bill for the gap.

sections.h2: What if Meade County tax is still owed when the house sells?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax does not vanish at closing. The County Clerk takes the bill after April 15 as a certificate, files a lien and adds interest of 1 percent per month. KRS 134.420 lets the lien last 11 years under any owner.

Two mailed notices come from the county attorney, the first within 30 days of the transfer and the second within 60. The sale falls between 90 and 135 days after the transfer, advertised 30 to 45 days ahead, and a buyer of the certificate may add substantial fees. Ask the Sheriff for a payoff through April 15 and the Clerk afterward, and have the closing agent pay from proceeds.

sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Meade County?
sections.html:
Created in 1823, Meade County spans 325 square miles, and its entire 56-mile northern boundary looks across the Ohio River at Indiana. Karst plains riddled with sinkholes cover much of the land, while the northwest rests on a plateau behind the Dripping Springs Escarpment. Brandenburg is the seat, Ekron and Muldraugh are the other cities, and Doe Valley and Fort Knox are census-designated places. Fort Knox is shared with Hardin County, and Meade belongs to the Louisville metro area with easy reach of the job centers at Elizabethtown and Fort Knox.

Meade County Schools, with Meade County High School, teaches most children. Families living on the Fort Knox base are zoned to the Defense Department's schools instead. The county keeps Eastern time, and Breckinridge County and Perry County, Indiana, to the west sit on Central time.

Workers travel a mean 33.0 minutes to their jobs. Owners live in 74.1 percent of homes, and 91.5 percent of households have broadband. The Census lists 2,790 veterans, 17.4 percent of residents at 65 or older, and a 91.0 percent high school graduation rate among adults. Poverty stands at 9.8 percent, against 13.9 percent in McCracken County. Sinkholes are common in this terrain, and a house with that problem or with deferred repairs can slow a conventional sale. A cash buyer who purchases as-is can close without those fixes.

faqs.q: Where do I pay the Meade County Sheriff?
faqs.a: At 516 Hillcrest Drive, Suite 14, Brandenburg, or by phone at (270) 422-4937. The PVA next door in Suite 3 never takes payments.

faqs.q: When does the Meade County Sheriff stop taking personal checks?
faqs.a: During the last two weeks before April 15. Cash, cards, money orders and cashier's checks are still accepted.

faqs.q: What was the 2026 homestead filing cutoff in Meade County?
faqs.a: May 22, 2026, for the exemption to show on the November bill. It has passed, so ask the PVA about the next cutoff.

faqs.q: How much state tax falls on a $207,900 Meade County house?
faqs.a: Close to $220.37 at the state's 2025 rate of 10.6 cents per $100. County and school levies come on top.

faqs.q: What becomes of Meade County bills left open after April 15?
faqs.a: They move to the County Clerk as certificates of delinquency, with a lien and 1 percent monthly interest. A sale can follow 90 to 135 days after the move.
